issues.legal_issue: A delayed writ challenge to land acquisition may be dismissed for laches where the delay is substantial and interference would cause public prejudice.
material_facts: The acquisition notifications were published in the official Gazette, and the challengers filed their writ petition nearly two and a half years later.

The challengers said they learned of the acquisition only when compensation notices were issued, but did not allege that the substance of the notification had not been publicly announced in the locality.
The challengers lived in the small locality where the lands were situated, and the Court considered it difficult to believe they remained unaware of the acquisition.
Interference at that stage was likely to cause serious public prejudice.
issues.conclusion: The challenge was liable to be dismissed on the ground of laches alone.
issues.legal_principle: A writ challenge brought after substantial delay may be rejected for laches, particularly where interference would cause serious public prejudice. The Court also applied the presumption that official acts have been duly performed, in the absence of an allegation that the required local public notice was not given.

rule.if: acquisition_writ_challenge and substantial_unexplained_delay and (local_residents_likely_aware or not_local_notice_failure_alleged) and interference_causes_public_prejudice

predicates.acquisition_writ_challenge: The proceeding is a writ challenge to a land acquisition.
predicates.substantial_unexplained_delay: The challenger waited a substantial period after publication before bringing the challenge without adequately explaining the delay.
predicates.local_residents_likely_aware: The challengers lived in a small locality where the acquisition was likely to become widely known.
predicates.not_local_notice_failure_alleged: The challengers did not allege that the substance of the acquisition notice had not been publicly announced in the locality.
predicates.interference_causes_public_prejudice: Interference with the acquisition at the time of the challenge would likely cause serious public prejudice.

issues.definition: When a land-acquisition writ challenge is substantially delayed, local awareness or the absence of an allegation that local notice was omitted, together with likely public prejudice from interference, supports dismissing the challenge for laches.

issues.legal_issue: A writ court should not interfere with an acquisition when the challengers' material claims depend on disputed questions of fact that they have not established.
material_facts: One challenger claimed that a house stood on a plot, but the respondents denied it and relied on records suggesting there was no house when the notification was issued.
Another challenger's claimed ownership was disputed because he was recorded as a co-holder with others who had not challenged the acquisition.
A further challenger had purchased a plot after the acquisition notifications were published.
The title claimed by another challenger was denied by the acquiring body's secretary.
issues.conclusion: The disputed factual questions meant that the challengers had not made out a case for interference under Article 226.
issues.legal_principle: The Court declined writ interference where the challengers' claims depended on disputed facts concerning the existence of a structure, ownership, or title. It distinguished State of Punjab v. Gurdial Singh, [1980] 1 S.C.R. 1071, because that case involved an allegation that the acquisition had been engineered mala fide, whereas no such allegation was made here.

predicates.acquisition_writ_challenge: The proceeding is a writ challenge to a land acquisition.
predicates.material_facts_disputed: The challengers' material claims about ownership, title, or the existence of a structure were denied or contradicted by the respondents' evidence.

issues.definition: When a land-acquisition writ challenge depends on material facts that the parties dispute, the challengers have not established a basis for writ interference on those facts.

issues.legal_issue: An urgency order dispensing with an opportunity to object to an acquisition is not invalid merely because construction of the public project was administratively delayed.
material_facts: Agricultural lands were acquired for construction of a market yard, and the Government treated the lands as urgently required for that public purpose.
The Government directed that the opportunity to object would not apply and authorized possession to be taken before an award was made.
There was some administrative delay in commencing construction, but construction had begun by the time of the appeal.
The challengers made no allegation that the acquisition had been engineered mala fide.
issues.conclusion: The administrative delay did not provide a ground to hold the urgency order invalid.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 17(4) and 5A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the Government may direct that the opportunity to object under section 5A will not apply in an urgent acquisition. The Court found no basis to invalidate that direction merely because of administrative delay in commencing construction. It distinguished State of Punjab v. Gurdial Singh, [1980] 1 S.C.R. 1071, where the acquisition was alleged to have been engineered mala fide.

rule.if: acquisition_writ_challenge and urgency_order_for_public_project and land_treated_as_urgently_required and administrative_delay_in_project and construction_commenced and not_mala_fide_allegation

predicates.acquisition_writ_challenge: The proceeding is a writ challenge to a land acquisition.
predicates.urgency_order_for_public_project: The Government issued an order dispensing with the opportunity to object and permitting early possession for a public project.
predicates.land_treated_as_urgently_required: The Government treated the land as urgently required for the public project.
predicates.administrative_delay_in_project: There was some administrative delay in commencing the project after the acquisition.
predicates.construction_commenced: Work on the public project had begun by the time the challenge was considered.
predicates.not_mala_fide_allegation: The challengers did not allege that the acquisition was engineered mala fide.

issues.definition: Where land is treated as urgently required for a public project and an urgency order is challenged, administrative delay does not invalidate the order when construction has commenced and no mala fide allegation is made.
